title: Cost Model service: add internal v1 endpoints (estimate, breakdown, what-if) with tenancy + request bounds
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Internal-only: Introduces Cost Model API v1 endpoints for estimate/breakdown/what-if with tenancy enforcement, bounded requests, and standard error codes. Console/Optimize adoption remains behind feature flags in follow-up PRs.
description: Summary: This PR introduces the Cost Model API v1 internal endpoints to support Console cost breakdown views and Optimize what-if projections, with consistent auth/tenancy enforcement and strict request bounding to avoid cardinality and latency blowups. Endpoints added (internal): 1) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/estimate: returns a per-request cost estimate (total + major components) for a single request context (model/runtime/deployment inputs + token counts + cache/batch/quant profile). Intended for hot-path per-request queries (Console drill-down, debugging). 2) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/breakdown: returns an aggregated bounded breakdown over a query window (e.g., per model, per route, per deployment mode) using pre-aggregated telemetry inputs. Designed for dashboards; supports pagination and server-side caps. 3) POST /internal/cost-model/v1/what-if: returns projections for config changes (batching/caching/quantization) given a workload summary. Includes an explicit confidence field and guardrails (range validation + scenario caps) to prevent expensive computations and misuse. Auth/tenancy: Enforces service-to-service auth via the internal gateway auth middleware; requires caller identity and verifies allowed service principals (Console, Optimize, and internal batch jobs). Adds required tenant scoping: org_id is mandatory; project_id optional depending on query type; all downstream telemetry/model-catalog reads are filtered by tenant scope. Adds auditing fields to logs (org_id, project_id, caller_service, schema_version) with PII-safe policies. Versioning/compatibility: v1 endpoints accept an explicit schema_version in the request (defaulting to latest supported v1.x). Response includes schema_version and server_build for debugging. Unknown fields are ignored (forward-compatible) but unknown schema_version returns 400 INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION with a supported_versions list in the message. Request bounds (perf + safety): estimate: max_input_tokens/max_output_tokens enforced (defaults: 128k input, 16k output); rejects negative/overflow; validates model_id + quant_profile_id exist in model catalog. breakdown: limits time window (max 31d), limits group_by keys (max 3), caps number of buckets returned (max 500), requires pagination token when truncated. what-if: caps scenarios (max 10), caps number of dimensions changed per scenario (max 3), validates allowed ranges for cache_hit_rate_delta, batch_size_target, and quant_profile_id. Also adds a server-side timeout budget with early exit returning partial results where applicable (explicit partial=true). Observability: Adds structured metrics and traces: cost_model_api_requests_total by endpoint + status, cost_model_api_latency_ms p50/p95, cost_model_api_bounds_rejections_total with reason, and cost_model_api_schema_version_distribution. Adds a trace span per endpoint with tags for org_id_hash (stable hash), caller_service, and schema_version. Error model: Standardizes error responses via Redwood API error envelope (code, message, request_id). Adds explicit codes: UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION, BOUNDS_EXCEEDED, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE (telemetry/model-catalog), and TIMEOUT. Note: this PR intentionally does not change billing hooks or Console/Optimize usage; those are follow-ups. Related: schema types were introduced in pr-28451; policy guardrails are further tuned in pr-28495; Console adoption tracked in ENG-4825 and Optimize adoption tracked in ENG-4826. Testing: Adds unit tests for request validation and tenancy filtering; contract tests for error codes; and a small integration test that runs the handlers against a stubbed telemetry store + model catalog. Includes golden response snapshots for the three endpoints. Rollout: Endpoints are behind the internal gateway route allowlist. No external exposure. Safe to deploy; no existing endpoints modified. Known limitations / follow-ups: - what-if currently models cache changes as a direct hit-rate delta; warm-rate modeling is deferred (see ENG-4824 comments). - breakdown endpoint uses pre-aggregated telemetry; per-request joins are intentionally not supported in v1 to keep performance bounded. - need to align with drift monitoring job once scheduled pipeline lands (ENG-4827).
commits: cost-model-service: add v1 router + handlers for estimate/breakdown/what-if
auth: enforce service principal allowlist + tenant scoping (org_id required)
validation: request bounds + schema version negotiation + error codes
observability: add endpoint metrics, trace spans, and structured logs
tests: unit + contract tests for tenancy, bounds, and error envelopes
review_conversation: Kaitlyn Nguyen (security): Tenancy scoping looks good, but we should require org_id for all endpoints, including breakdown where project_id is optional. Also please add caller_service to audit logs. Ethan Park (author): Updated validation to require org_id across the board and added caller_service from auth context to structured logs + traces. Added tests for missing org_id returning INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Logan Wright (telemetry): For breakdown, please ensure group_by values are a fixed allowlist; we cannot accept arbitrary tag keys or we’ll blow up cardinality. Ethan Park (author): Added allowlist for group_by (model_id, route, deployment_mode, region, quant_profile_id) and hard cap of 3 keys. Added BOUNDS_EXCEEDED on violations and metrics for rejection reasons.

Chloe Martin (Console): On hot paths, Console needs predictable response sizes; can we guarantee max buckets and include a next_page_token when truncated? Ethan Park (author): Implemented bucket cap 500 with deterministic sorting, added next_page_token + truncated flag, and documented pagination contract in internal docs.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Please add explicit timeout handling and surface when results are partial. Also would like a metric for bounds rejections and upstream failures. Ethan Park (author): Added server timeout budget per endpoint, partial=true where applicable (what-if); exported cost_model_api_bounds_rejections_total and cost_model_api_upstream_failures_total.

Benji Okafor (platform): Endpoint names OK. One nit: error code INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION should list supported versions in message. Ethan Park (author): Done. Error message now includes supported_versions=["cost-model/v1.0","cost-model/v1.1"].
